input.quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
input.rationale:
The IP bargain runs in our favour and meets the preferred position on its material terms. Section 13.1 (p0197) gives IBM ownership of, and MSL a present and future assignment of, all intellectual and industrial property rights in the hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered; p0198 extends IBM ownership/MSL assignment to MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes and systems, with MSL's retained use limited to performing its obligations here. Ownership is stronger than the fallback licence, so the fallback licence elements (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use, modification and sublicensing) are subsumed. MSL keeps generic production tooling (p1088: "Tools commonly used in production and/or Integration will be owned and managed by MSL"), which the playbook expressly permits. Any MSL licence in IBM information is confined to service delivery: 13.3(a) (p0208) grants MSL only a royalty-free licence to use confidential information disclosed under the AECI "necessary to manufacture Products solely for IBM", and any other licence to IBM IP requires a separate signed agreement; IBM documentation and confidential media must be returned on termination (p0130). There is no joint ownership and no assignment of IBM IP or data to MSL, so no walk-away trigger. Minor points noted only, not redlined: there is no express "MSL retains its pre-existing IP" sentence (a Vendor-side omission that does not prejudice us), no standalone Customer Data ownership sentence, and 24.1(a) (p1136) says MSL conveys no licence under its own IP in the I/T systems context, which is overridden for delivered Products by the 13.1 assignment. The AECI residuals clause (p1482) is a confidentiality mechanic reviewed under that rule, not IP.</rationale>
</invoke>
